title: Praying with Jane Eyre
author: Vanessa Zoltan
description: a book that's part memoir and part guide to reading any book as a sacred text

title: To Carve a Fae Heart
author: Tessonja Odette
description: To Carve a Fae Heart is an enemies-to-lovers fantasy, perfect for fans of The Cruel Prince, ACOTAR, and Kingdom of the Wicked. If you like snarky fae, brooding royals, sizzling romance, and fierce heroines, you'll love this breathtaking fae fantasy. *NOTE: This series is Upper YA/NA and contains sexual situations, moderate steam, and some violence.

title: The Witch Boy
author: Molly Knox Ostertag
description: middle-grade graphic novel about a boy in a magical family learning witchcraft, challenging family tradition, and going on an adventure.

title: How Stella Learned to Talk
author: Christina Hunger
description: An incredible, revolutionary true story and surprisingly simple guide to teaching your dog to talk from speech-language pathologist Christina Hunger, who has taught her dog, Stella, to communicate using simple paw-sized buttons associated with different words.

title: Divine Rivals
author: Rebecca Ross
description: When two young rival journalists find love through a magical connection, they must face the depths of hell, in a war among gods, to seal their fate forever.

title: Ruthless Vows
author: Rebecca Ross
description: The epic conclusion to Divine Rivals

title: So You Want to Talk About Race
author: Ijeoma Oluo
description: An exploration of 2018's racial landscape with actionable advice for talking about race in uncomfortable contexts and circumstances

title: Learn You a Haskell for Great Good: A Beginner's Guide
author: Miran Lipovaca
description: A guided walkthrough through learning the haskell programming language and functional programming paradigms

title: Hidden Memory
author: Tiffany Shearn
description: "Elves, fairy, and an epic war between good and evil"

title: Witch Child
author: Celia Rees
description: "The spellbinding diary of a teenage girl who escapes persecution as a witch--only to face new intolerance in a Puritan settlement. "

title: Thug Kitchen: the official cookbook
author: Thug Kitchen
description: a cookbook of vegan recipes. I'm not vegan and it was fun to try out some new recipes using ingredients and techniques I hadn't known about before. The writing style is quite tiresome but the content is good.

title: Unix: in a Nutshell
author: Arnold Robbins
description: A cool desk reference for those who want to learn about or work regularly with unix systems. I got this in my undergrad and it served me well.
